name: Ejiro Evero

views.text: Rotate the front so your best linemen are still fresh in the fourth quarter and in December.
A versatile tackle who can line up anywhere is how you create mismatches up front.
Players who already speak the language of the system make a new defense move faster.
Bringing back players you have coached is about smarts and toughness, not familiarity for its own sake.
When injuries gut the roster, you keep teaching and keep the standard; you do not change who you are.
The best defensive rooms are partly coached by the veterans in them.
Effort is the one thing on tape you never have to coach twice.

signatures: praises a lineman's effort and versatility with specific alignments rather than stats
talks about the meeting room's level of conversation as a sign of progress
credits veteran players who help coach the younger ones
want: to turn a defense that hit historic lows into a respected unit and earn a head-coaching job on that turnaround
fear: that one record-setting bad season becomes the only thing people remember about his defenses
voice: Measured, polite and even-toned, he talks football in specifics: alignments, rotations and how a player wins his matchup. He praises effort and the veterans who help teach, and he does not sound rattled when results are poor. He avoids big claims and keeps his answers on the unit.

evidence.summary: Denver hires him from the Rams, where he spent five seasons ending as secondary coach and pass game coordinator; his first job calling plays. He and head coach Hackett were UC Davis teammates and close friends, and he was in Hackett's wedding. Background, no quotes on style.

Head-coach interview note: career path from UC Davis through Tampa Bay, San Francisco and Green Bay to the Rams under McVay (2017-2021), then a strong 2022 in Denver (sixth in yards per play, second on third down). No personality detail.

After the opener he praises Derrick Brown's run defense, pursuit and stamina, notes he can line up over tight ends, guards or centers, and explains wanting a rotating front to keep starters fresh. Team-site; reporter calls him measured and upbeat.
Canales retains Evero, saying his defenses were hard to face from the offensive side and he wants to learn the system. Shows the staffing decision and Canales's respect.

evidence.publisher: Panthers Wire via Yahoo Sports, Anthony Rizzuti
evidence.summary: He discusses signing players he coached before (Jewell from Denver; Robinson, Fuller, Scott from the Rams), calling them smart, tough and effortful, while noting the Carolina defense will differ from earlier versions so roles will too. His words, fan-network outlet.

Early in the offseason he says meeting-room talk is sharp across groups, shared system language puts the defense ahead of last year, and Derrick Brown is already helping coach the line room while Clowney's feedback helps young players. Team-site.

Recaps a 2024 defense that allowed a record 534 points amid injuries, notes Canales publicly backed and retained him, and frames 2025 as a possible last stand after defensive additions. Portrays him as steady but does not describe his personality directly.

evidence.publisher: Carolina Panthers (panthers.com), Darin Gantt and Kassidy Hill
evidence.summary: Evero says Brown looks like his 2023 Pro Bowl self after a lost 2024, describes him as hard to block one-on-one, and praises his growing leadership in holding teammates and coaches accountable. Short quotes on one player.
